mission_section: 1-2: mandatory numerical audit + official/numerical status split
method: 9 representative delays (29.8600-29.8665s) x 5 diagnostic timesteps (0.05/0.02/0.01/0.005/0.001s), full field extraction per scripts/phase5b_numerical_convergence.py, raw data in booster-numerical-convergence.json and booster-contact-mode-map.json
finding: CATEGORICAL, NOT MARGINAL. Every one of the 8 delays that produced a <5 m/s (legal) touchdown at the official 0.05s timestep produces a 10.6-14.6 m/s (illegal, ~3x over threshold) touchdown at ALL FOUR finer timesteps tested (0.02, 0.01, 0.005, 0.001s), with no exceptions. The 9th delay (29.866s) was illegal at every timestep including 0.05s, and is the only one of the 9 that 'agrees' across timesteps -- trivially, since it never claimed legality. Illegal-side touchdown speeds are internally consistent and roughly monotonic across delay at a fixed timestep (e.g. all ~11 m/s at 0.02s, all ~12-12.4 m/s at 0.01s, all ~14-14.6 m/s at 0.005s, all ~10.6-10.9 m/s at 0.001s) -- this is a real, reproducible dynamical result at fine resolution, not scattered noise.
likely_mechanism: burn_remaining_at_contact_s at the reference point was previously measured at ~0.39s (booster-relative-timing-model.json). At the official 0.05s fixed timestep, only ~8 integration samples span that entire critical burn-to-contact interval; at 0.001s there are ~390. The 0.05s step is very likely too coarse to resolve the exact ground-contact/thrust interaction, and/or interacts badly with the discrete anti-tumble JavaScript listener's per-step control logic (not isolated by this audit -- flagged as an open question, not settled).
official_setting_authority_status: AUTHORITY-LEGAL (unchanged from phase5a's own basin characterization: rule-legal, non-monotonic, 8-9/9 tested delays <5 m/s at the configured 0.05s timestep)
classification_rationale: SOLVER-SENSITIVE would describe partial/marginal disagreement (some delays converge, some don't, or touchdown speed shifts by tens of percent near the legal boundary). What was measured instead is a 100% reversal rate (8/8 legal points become illegal, by a factor of ~3x, at every single finer timestep tried) with no delay in the tested set surviving refinement. This meets the 'AUTHORITY RESULT INVALIDATED' bar, not 'SOLVER-SENSITIVE'.
consequence_for_prior_claims: The 'LEGAL BOOSTER BRANCH RECOVERED' classification in artifacts/autoevo/phase4c-summary.json, .planning/.continue-here.md, and handoff.md was based exclusively on the official 0.05s timestep. This audit does not identify a new bug in the extraction pipeline (touchdown speed reuses the same GROUND_HIT-interpolated run_sim() path used throughout the whole codebase, unmodified here) -- it shows the underlying OpenRocket dynamical result at that timestep does not reproduce under timestep refinement. Per the mission's own instruction ('Do not call the booster basin physically robust until the timestep audit passes'), the booster branch cannot currently be treated as a legal recovered branch for calibration or full-vehicle-authority purposes until this is resolved.
open_questions_before_further_action: Is the official 0.05s timestep itself an intentional, rules-compliant simulation setting (i.e. is coarse timestep the officially sanctioned/submitted configuration, making the fine-timestep result irrelevant to the actual competition scoring), or was 0.05s simply an unexamined default inherited from earlier sessions?
Does the anti-tumble JavaScript listener's behavior depend on step count/timing in a way that could itself explain the divergence (untested by this audit)?
Is convergence reached at any resolution finer than 0.001s, or does the touchdown speed keep changing (true non-convergence vs. a slow monotonic approach to a different limit)?
recommendation: Do not proceed to treat the booster branch as a calibration positive control (mission section 4) or resume any coupled/full-vehicle authority claim until: (a) it is confirmed whether 0.05s is the rules-mandated/submission timestep, and (b) if finer timestep is the correct standard, a NEW delay search is run at a converged timestep before any legal claim is made.
